articles.title: HBO's 'Harry Potter' series cast: Meet the new generation of stars headed to Hogwarts in 4 months
articles.summary: The first season will premiere Dec. 25, and HBO has already renewed the series for Season 2.
articles.body:
Can you feel the magic? The Harry Potter franchise is expanding once again with HBO's Harry Potter TV series, set to premiere Dec. 25.

The show has a lot to live up to, given the success of J.K. Rowling's book series and the Warner Bros. movie adaptations. But fans have shown excitement as HBO has revealed the sprawling cast bringing a new generation of beloved characters to the screen.

The first season has finished filming at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden in the U.K., where the original movie franchise was filmed from 2000 to 2010 . Each season will focus on one of the seven books.

HBO has already renewed the series for Season 2, which will adapt Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. Game of Thrones star Kit Harington will be among the new faces at Hogwarts.

The episodes are being written and executive-produced by Francesca Gardiner, whose credits include HBO's drama Succession and the BBC's spy thriller Killing Eve. Mark Mylod, who also worked on Succession , will direct several episodes. Jon Brown has been named co-showrunner alongside Gardiner for Season 2.

Here's what we know so far about the cast.

McLaughlin will be playing the iconic role of Harry Potter. Daniel Radcliffe starred as the character from 2001 through 2011. The Scottish actor, who is 12 years old, also appeared in the BBC series Gifted and Sky original film Grow .

Twelve-year-old Stanton will play Hermione Granger, one of the brightest witches of her generation. The character was previously played by Emma Watson in all eight Harry Potter films. This is Stanton's first onscreen role, having previously starred in Matilda on London's West End in 2023.

Stout will play Ron Weasley, the sixth and youngest son in the Weasley family. Rupert Grint originated the role, starting when he was just 11 years old. According to Stout's online actor profile , this will be his first onscreen acting role after previously being cast in a commercial for Albert Bartlett potatoes.

Pratt will play Slytherin antagonist Draco Malfoy, who was portrayed by Tom Felton in the films. The young British actor also starred as one of the lead characters in the BBC's adaptation of Lord of the Flies , William Golding's 1954 novel.

Lithgow will play Albus Dumbledore, the headmaster of Hogwarts. The character has previously been played by Richard Harris and Michael Gambon in the Harry Potter franchise and Jude Law and Toby Regbo in the Fantastic Beasts series.

"Well, it came as a total surprise to me," Lithgow told ScreenRant in February 2025. "I just got the phone call up at the Sundance Film Festival for yet another film, and it was not an easy decision because it's going to define me for the last chapter of my life, I'm afraid. But I'm very excited. Some wonderful people are turning their attention back to Harry Potter. That's why it's been such a hard decision. I'll be about 87 years old at the wrap party, but I've said yes."

The British actor has been cast as Severus Snape, the potions professor at Hogwarts. Alan Rickman played Snape in all eight Harry Potter films. Essiedu earned several nominations for his role in the BBC's I May Destroy You and costarred with Saoirse Ronan in The Outrun, which premiered at the 2024 Sundance Film Festival.

McTeer will play Professor McGonagall, the head of Gryffindor House and the deputy headmistress under Dumbledore. Maggie Smith played McGonagall in the Harry Potter movies, while Fiona Glascott played her in Fantastic Beasts. McTeer has won multiple theater, film and TV awards and nominations and starred in 2025's Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning with Tom Cruise.

Frost has been cast as Rubeus Hagrid, a half-giant who works as the groundskeeper at Hogwarts. Robbie Coltrane originated the character in the Harry Potter movies. Frost is most well known for his involvement in Shaun of the Dead, Hot Fuzz and World's End.

Whitehouse will play Argus Filch, the caretaker at Hogwarts, who was portrayed by David Bradley in every Harry Potter film. The British actor was one of the main stars of the BBC sketch comedy show The Fast Show , which ran from 1994 to 2014.

The British stage actor will play Quirinus Quirrell, the Defense Against the Dark Arts professor for the first book and movie, which means Thallon will only be in the first season of the show. Ian Hart played Quirrell in Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone . Thallon has played the lead in multiple major stage productions in London.

Flynn has been cast as Draco Malfoy's father, Lucius Malfoy, previously played by Jason Isaacs. Flynn starred in Netflix's sitcom Lovesick and is also known for his performances as David Bowie in Stardust and George Knightley in Emma , an adaptation of the Jane Austen novel. Isaacs, who played Lucius in the original Harry Potter films, reacted to the casting in a post on Instagram on June 9, saying he was "thrilled to be passing the keys to Malfoy Manor" and called Flynn "a brilliant actor."

Powley will be playing Harry's aunt Petunia Dursley, originally portrayed by Fiona Shaw. Powley's known for her roles in The Diary of a Teenage Girl and The Morning Show .

Rigby will play Harry's uncle Vernon Dursley, who was played by the actor Richard Griffiths in the original films. Rigby's acting history is a mix of stage theater, stand-up comedy, films and TV. On Instagram , the comedian said he was "thrilled to be playing the world's worst muggle, Uncle Vernon."

Parkinson will play Ron Weasley's mom, Molly Weasley, who was previously played by Julie Walters. Parkinson rose to prominence with her role in the British comedy series The IT Crowd , which earned her two BAFTA awards for Best Female Comedy Performance in 2009 and 2014. She's most recently starred in the hit TV show Rivals .

Game of Thrones star Harington will play Gilderoy Lockhart, the wizard who becomes Hogwarts' Defense Against the Dark Arts professor in Chamber of Secrets . Kenneth Branagh originally portrayed the character in the 2002 film. He replaces Nicholas Hoult, who was initially cast in the role but left the series due to scheduling conflicts.

Warwick Davis, who played two different characters in the movies, is reprising one of his roles — as Charms Professor Filius Flitwick, HBO announced last year. Davis is the first actor from the original Harry Potter films playing the same character in the upcoming series.

"Hogwarts has always held a very special place in my heart," Davis wrote in an Instagram caption after the casting announcement was made. "Thank you to all the fans who have kept the magic alive — I can't wait to see you back in the classroom. Here's to further adventures at Hogwarts."

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry, told ComicBook in June 2023 that he supported the new show but was not interested in being involved.

"I'm definitely not seeking it out in any way," he said. "But I do wish them, obviously, all the luck in the world, and I'm very excited to have that torch passed. But I don't think it needs me to physically pass it."

Several actors involved in the film series — Rickman, Coltrane, Gambon and Smith — have since died.

HBO has unveiled more cast members who will play minor — but still memorable — characters in the upcoming TV show.

William Nash is Draco Malfoy's Slytherin friend Gregory Goyle, played by Josh Herdman in the movies.

Finn Stephens is Malfoy's other friend Vincent Crabbe, originally played by Jamie Waylett.

Elijah Oshin is the fellow Gryffindor Dean Thomas, previously played by Alfred Enoch.

Bríd Brennan is the Hogwarts healer Madam Poppy Pomfrey, originally played by Gemma Jones.

Richard Durden has been cast as History of Magic Professor Cuthbert Binns, a character who was not portrayed in the original Harry Potter movies.

Sirine Saba is Herbology Professor Pomona Sprout, who was played by Miriam Margolyes.

Leigh Gill is playing the Gringotts goblin banker Griphook, previously played by Warwick Davis (who also played Professor Flitwick).

Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, originally played by James Phelps.

Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, formerly played by Oliver Phelps.

Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, played by Chris Rankin in the movies.

Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley, originally portrayed by Bonnie Wright. She will be recast in Season 2 "due to unforeseen circumstances."

Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, originally played by Matthew Lewis.

Amos Kitson is playing Dudley Dursley, who was played by Harry Melling in the movies.

Louise Brealey as Madam Rolanda Hooch, previously played by Zoë Wanamaker.

Anton Lesser is Garrick Ollivander, formerly played by John Hurt.

Leo Earley is Seamus Finnigan, previously portrayed by Devon Murray.

Alessia Leoni is Parvati Patil, originally played by Shefali Chowdhury.

Sienna Moosah is Lavender Brown, played by Jessie Cave in the films.

Bertie Carvel will play Minister for Magic Cornelius Fudge, who was previously played by Robert Hardy.

Is J.K. Rowling involved in the TV show?

Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav said that he and HBO and Max executives Casey Bloys and Channing Dungey have met with author J.K. Rowling about the reboot.

"We spent some real time with J.K. and her team," Zaslav said during a Warner Bros. company call in December. "Both sides are thrilled to be reigniting this franchise. Our conversations were great, and we couldn't be more excited about what's ahead."

In a Warner Bros. press release in 2023, Rowling said, "Max's commitment to preserving the integrity of my books is important to me, and I'm looking forward to being part of this new adaptation, which will allow for a degree of depth and detail only afforded by a long-form television series."

Bloys told IndieWire in November 2024 that Rowling has "been fairly involved in the process of selecting the writer and director" of the TV show and will "have opinions on casting."

In an April 2025 episode of The Town podcast , which covers Hollywood news, Bloys defended HBO's decision to continue working with Rowling on the show after some fans raised concerns over her political beliefs .

"The decision to be in business with J.K. Rowling is not new for us," Bloys said. "We've been in business for 25 years. We already have a show on HBO from her called C.B. Strike that we do with the BBC. It's pretty clear that those are her personal, political views. She's entitled to them. Harry Potter is not secretly being infused with anything. And if you want to debate her, you can go on Twitter."

Fan concerns about Rowling's involvement have popped up multiple times since the new series was announced. In April 2025, Essiedu, who was cast as Snape, along with Eddie Redmayne, who starred in Fantastic Beasts, and Katie Leung, who was in the original Harry Potter films, signed an open letter calling on the U.K.'s entertainment industry to protect the transgender community.

While Rowling condemned the petition on X, she later responded directly to speculation she would fire Essiedu from the new series, writing: "I don't have the power to sack an actor from the series, and I wouldn't exercise it if I did. I don't believe in taking away people's jobs or livelihoods because they hold legally protected beliefs that differ from mine."

articles.title: Life360 expands pet tracking with new $8 scannable tags and zoomie alerts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Life360’s new $7.99 scannable pet tags alert families when a lost pet is found and share its last known location, while new care-tracking features help households keep tabs on feeding, walks, medication, and more.
articles.body:
Family location-sharing and safety app Life360 is expanding its pet-tracking capabilities on Tuesday with the launch of a new product line of $7.99 scannable pet tags and other pet-care features that tap into its tracking network technology.

Life360 expanded into pet tech last year with the launch of GPS pet trackers that leverage the lost-item-finding capabilities that the company integrated into its platform after its 2021 acquisition of AirTag rival Tile. With Tile, the company now offers not just location-sharing features for families, but also the ability for members to track other things of importance — like keys, handbags, luggage, and pets.

Since then, families on the service have added more than 8 million pets to their accounts, the company says.

However, the team found that not everyone wants to attach a bulky tracker to their pet’s collar, and not everyone needs access to location-tracking features or other advanced options like geofences and escape alerts.

In many cases, pet owners just want to put their contact information on a pet’s tag, which is what the new scannable pet tags support.

But there’s a twist. Instead of just providing a pet owner’s phone number when someone scans the QR code printed on the new pet tags, the scan also alerts the family through the Life360 app installed on the family’s smartphones. (The person who found the pet does not need to have the app for this to work.)

This helps in multiple ways — not only does it provide peace of mind to families searching for a lost pet, but it also provides the pet’s location details. That can be useful if the lost pet escapes from the finder’s control and runs off again, as the family will at least have the last known location recorded.

Families can update their contact details through the Life360 pet profile in the app.

In addition, the company is rolling out several new pet-care features for families, including tools that let families schedule “care logs” to manage and track whether the pet has been fed, walked, given medication, or had its litter cleaned. Everyone in the family can see these care routines, so they will know if the pet needs their attention.

Another fun feature is “Zoomies Alerts” for GPS trackers, which track the bursts of energy a pet has at particular points during the day or evening. A new Weekly Roundup will recap other routines, like the distance walked or information about who in the family provided the pet with the most care during the week.

With the new features, the company is also making its pet trackers more affordable. Before, the Pet GPS trackers were only available with the higher-tier Platinum and Gold subscriptions, but now they’re included with the $99-per-year Silver bundles, too.

The new pet tags and GPS trackers are sold on both the company’s website and Amazon in the U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the U.K.

articles.title: As if drivers in LA weren’t bad enough.
articles.summary:
NBC News identified 43 videos that appear to show Tesla drivers asleep at the wheel, 17 of which were posted this year alone. This is, of course, a well-worn problem for Tesla, which has tried to curb the trend with stricter driver monitoring systems. But drivers are easily subverting these guardrails with sunglasses, allowing them to continue sleeping despite eye-tracking technology.

articles.title: Nothing OS 5.0 brings a new Glyph Interface app and a more customizable homescreen
articles.summary: Nothing OS 5.0 introduces Android 17 features, a new glyph app, and a redesigned homescreen starting with an open beta on August 26th.
articles.body: With the new design of Nothing OS 5.0, app icons and widgets can use adaptive color to get color tints pulled from your wallpaper, which update whenever your wallpaper changes. Alongside Android’s built-in Dynamic Colors, the company says it allows you to have specific elements change to match your wallpaper “while Nothing’s predominantly monochrome character stays underneath.”  While I like Nothing’s simplified, monochrome app icons, it’s nice to get an option for adding some limited areas of color to the homescreen. Nothing’s launching it as “an additional theme,” so you can keep using the old design if you like. The Android 17-based update is launching in open beta on August 26th, starting with the Nothing Phone 3. It will eventually also roll out to most of Nothing’s other phones, but a few older devices aren’t getting this update, including the Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 — the last of which I’ve been using, so unfortunately I won’t get to try out these new features myself. [Image: Most Nothing phones will get the update by January 2027. The latest version of Nothing OS also adds a slew of new homescreen customization options and quality-of-life tweaks that will let you track how long you spend away from your phone, or make better use of its Essential AI features. And if you have a Nothing phone with its glyph interface lighting, a new dedicated app pulls all the features and controls into one spot. [Image: You can control Nothing’s glyph lights from a dedicated app now. Lockscreen clockfaces can also use colors from your wallpaper now. There are also a couple of new lockscreen clockfaces in Nothing OS 5.0, including a bubbly “Gooey” design and an information-dense “Micrographics” one.  Since Nothing OS 5.0 is built on Android 17, it also includes platform updates like enhanced quick share, Android’s new Noto 3D emojis, and expanded dark theme support. Other new highlights include:  * “Geist” system typeface * Away Time widget that tracks how long you haven’t been using your phone, and Collector widget that turns pictures of items into home or lock screen icons * Select multiple homescreen app icons to move them all at once * Status bar icons with animations to signify things like turning airplane mode on or off * Single-tap Bluetooth controls in Quick Settings  * Essential AI updates including support for Model Context Protocol (MCP), cleaner transcriptions from Essential Voice, a Smart Collections feature for organizing Essential Space captures, and support for building Essential Apps on-device

articles.title: Bose’s smallest Bluetooth speaker is a great deal at 35 percent off
articles.summary: In addition to the Bose Soundlink Micro, we found discounts on a 5TB Seagate external hard drive, the refurbished Apple Watch Series 9, and the Ultraloq Bolt.
articles.body: Bose may be best known for its QuietComfort headphones, but the brand’s Bluetooth speakers have earned a great reputation for featuring great sound and build quality. The compact Bose SoundLink Micro — its most compact Bluetooth speaker — is currently discounted to $79.99 at Amazon, a pretty great discount from its usual $129 price tag. [Product: Bose SoundLink Micro Portable Speaker (2nd Gen) | The rounded-off square speaker is almost pocketable, and easily slides into a purse or backpack; it’s just over four inches wide, 1.54 inches deep, and weighs less than a pound. It’s dustproof and waterproof, with an IP67 rating that matches the larger Bose Bluetooth speakers, and should last a full day at the beach or by the pool. The speaker will run for up to 12 hours on a single charge, and has convenient nylon strap for attaching it to your backpack or to your bike’s handlebars. Other deals to consider * Best Buy has the 5TB Seagate Game Drive discounted to $169.99 (usually $219.99) until the end of the day. While it might seem odd to buy a non-SSD external drive in 2026, the price here is better than we’ve seen recently for this capacity. This model is compatible with computers as well as Xbox consoles, although only games predating the Xbox Series S/X era will be able to be played directly from the drive. Newer games will need to first be copied over to your console’s speedy SSD. * Woot is selling a variety of refurbished Apple Watch Series 9 units for as low as $189.99, depending on the configuration you choose. While they’re a couple of generations old, it’s rare to see recent models that low, and this is one of the older Apple Watches that will support watchOS 27. Woot is covering the devices with a one year warranty in case there are any issues down the road. Read our review. * Until the end of the day, you can grab an Ultraloq Bolt door lock for $74.99 from Amazon (usually $109.99). This Wi-Fi smart lock features both numerical and fingerprint sensors, giving you a few options for quickly unlocking your door. You can check the status and lock or unlock the door from your phone, and it integrates with other smart home platforms like Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home.

articles.title: Dreame’s dream of a rocket-powered car is dead
articles.summary: Dreame’s rocket-boosted car project is shutting down, after China’s government decided to take a harder look at the vacuum company’s ambitious ventures.
articles.body: Dreame, the Chinese vacuum company that aspires to be a global technology giant, is reportedly shutting down its automotive project after funding from the government dried up. According to CarNewsChina, the company’s automotive division called “Project Starry Sky” once employed over 1,000 people, but now only a handful legal and HR staffers remain, charged with winding down the operation. In a statement, Dreame said it “recently adjusted certain operations that were in the exploratory phase,” and that going forward, it would focus on four key business areas: “smart home, outdoor/garden, smart mobility, and embodied AI.” (A spokesperson for the company didn’t respond to a request for comment.) The news comes after China’s government issued new rules aimed at tightening oversight of the $3.4 trillion private fund industry, singling out Dreame in the process. After becoming one of the world’s largest manufacturer of vacuums, the company quickly moved into a variety of new businesses, spawning nearly a thousand affiliated ventures related to smartphones, robotics, and cars. But much of that expansion was funded by China’s government — and the government is now starting to take a closer look at how Dreame spends that money, according to CNBC. [Image: The NEXT 01 JET Edition Car at the Dreame NEXT event during the Silicon Valley Summit at the Palace of Fine Arts on April 29, 2026 in San Francisco, CA. Dreame wowed audiences at a San Francisco expo earlier this year with “Nebula Next 01 Jet Edition,” a sleek looking concept car equipped with a pair of rocket engines that theoretically can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 0.9 seconds. The vehicle was allegedly equipped with a sulfide-based solid-state battery with a record-breaking energy density exceeding 450 Wh/kg and a purported range of over 550 km (341.7 miles). The company claimed its boosters would deliver 100 kilo-Newtons of force. But the concept raised a lot of questions, including some basic ones about how Dreame could make a car accelerate so quickly without breaking the laws of physics. Apparently Dreame didn’t have any answers to these questions, as the car itself was fully vaporware. Former employees told China Economy that the concept that was shown off in San Francisco lacked an actual chassis and was driven via remote control. (Concept cars are rarely “real” cars, in the technical sense — but even this is a little shocking in its level of deception.) The news that Dreame’s vaporware car was totally vaporware will come as little shock to those familiar with the showy, boastful promises of companies that have never actually built a car suddenly deciding to build a car. Faraday Future, another Chinese companies with ambitions to build all manner of electric, autonomous vehicles, ran into this exact problem nearly a decade ago. And it also faced accusations of operating self-driving cars for public demos via offstage remote control.

articles.title: At just $8, you owe it to yourself to grab Inscryption
articles.summary: Humble has the creepy genre-bending deckbuilder on sale for $7.99, just two dollars higher than its all-time low price.
articles.body: If you watched the Gamescom 2026 announcements, you might have caught a trailer for the bizarre, frenetic Pony Island 2: Panda Circus, a game from Daniel Mullins. In case you haven’t heard of him, get a crash course with a fantastic discount on Inscryption. Humble is currently selling Steam versions of the secret-packed deckbuilder for $7.99, a sizable discount from its usual price of $20. It’s compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux machines. [Product: Inscryption | The game starts out as a fairly straightforward deckbuilding roguelike game with a dark atmosphere. Stick with it, and it’ll evolve, defying genres, breaking the fourth wall, and leading you through a twisted story with plenty of surprises. Part of the fun is discovering those twists yourself, so I won’t say anything else. It’s one of my personal favorite games, and it’s best to go in knowing as little as possible. Thankfully, taking the leap isn’t expensive at all. Read our Inscryption review.

articles.title: Garmin’s new Fenix 9 adds brighter screens and smoother map panning
articles.summary: Garmin just launched its Fenix 9 and 9 Pro smartwatches, both of which come with brighter OLED displays. The Fenix 9 Pro model also offers satellite connectivity across all three size options.
articles.body: Garmin just took the wraps off its new line of rugged Fenix 9 smartwatches, with the base model featuring an OLED display with a brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making it twice as bright as its predecessor. Starting at $999.99 for the 43mm case option, the Fenix 9 has 50 percent more RAM and an upgraded map engine, allowing for faster panning. It also comes with a scratch-resistant sapphire lens, an increased 64GB of storage, and a bunch of new software-based features, like Garmin Epic. This feature groups all the workouts you’ve done over several days, weeks, or months to create an “Epic” that shows your health and performance data within that period. There are also new stamina tracking metrics and expanded rucking features that let you change the weight of your pack during a workout. Garmin says the Fenix 9 offers up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode on the largest 51mm size. [Image: [Image: [Image: The Fenix 9 Pro starts at $1,099.99 and expands on these upgrades with a new titanium case. It has InReach satellite or LTE connectivity available on all three 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm options for an extra $100 and a $7.99 / month subscription. The largest Fenix 9 Pro variation also offers a 1.5-inch OLED display for the first time. That’s just a little bigger than the 1.3-inch and 1.4-inch displays available with the smaller case sizes across the Fenix 9 lineup. [Image: [Image: [Image: Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option that promises up to 57 days of battery life (with the caveat that you spend three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions).  The Fenix 9 lineup is available in an array of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.

articles.title: How Modern Appointment Viewing Shows Are Bringing Back ‘Watercooler’ Television
articles.summary: There’s nothing better than sitting on the couch to binge your favorite TV show. Or, maybe, there is. In the era of streaming, binge-watching is easier than...
articles.body:
There's nothing better than sitting on the couch to binge your favorite TV show. Or, maybe, there is. In the era of streaming, binge-watching is easier than ever. So, it seems potentially incongruous that appointment viewing — watching a television show when it first airs — is so capable of seizing the collective attention of viewers.

But fandom is a powerful force, and appointment viewing has tamed the beast into something fearsome. Rather than encouraging viewers to settle in with episode after episode queued up, shows like "Survivor," "The Pitt" and summer's guilty pleasure "Love Island" make their fans wait for it.

How 'The Pitt' Production Designer Expanded the Emergency Room for Season 2

'Survivor' vs. 'The Traitors': Will Emmy Voters Finally Give the Original Reality Juggernaut Its Due?

'The Pitt' Season 3 Trailer: Dr. Robby's First Day Back Is Filled With More Medical Emergencies

It's not a new concept; "Survivor" has been rocking weekly episode drops since its first foray in 2000 on the Bornean beaches. But it has reached a new fervor with watch parties popping up across the country and "Love Island'"s reality flair convincing millions to watch almost daily as hot singles couple up.

There's obvious incentive to watch when an episode airs if everyone is talking about it; you can hardly open your phone during "Love Island" season without seeing a spoiler. And the reality dating show takes it a step further: Fans can vote live on who must leave the villa and who lives to flirt another day.

"Survivor" has dabbled in the fan vote mechanism, too. An extra prize in "Survivor: All-Stars," casting selection for "Survivor: Cambodia — Second Chance" and gameplay elements in "Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans" were all left, well, in the hands of the fans.

Even a non-reality show like "The Pitt" has capitalized on the power behind scheduled releases. The first two episodes of Season 1 dropped concurrently on Jan. 9, 2025, but every subsequent episode has been released on a weekly schedule.

As with any show that received such critical esteem as the Pittsburgh-based medical drama, whose first season won five of its 13 Emmy nominations, Season 2 was accused online of a sophomore slump. Those critical social media fans were accused right back of not watching as intended (i.e., bandwagon binge-ing Season 1 and being upset about starting Season 2 before that was possible).

"Survivor" showrunner and Emmy-nominated host Jeff Probst describes the difference between binge-watching and appointment viewing as the difference between a flight and a road trip. Both get you to the destination, but with one, the time spent is part of the experience.

Viewers had a week to reckon with the knowledge that there was an active shooter event in the first season of "The Pitt" before the fallout reached the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center in the next episode. Skipping a night of "Love Island" this summer might have meant a fan's favorite couple exiting the villa — and certainly meant not understanding the social media memes and reactions the next day. Sure, you can binge old seasons of "Survivor," but you lose the emotional experience of living with Probst snuffing the torch of a beloved player.

The time between episodes is where fandom finds its home: reacting, interacting and generally causing a stir around a show in a way that binge-watches can't always pull off. "The Pitt" has been lauded as a return to classic television, the kind of "water cooler" show that inspires next-day conversations with coworkers.

"That waiting period creates a different kind of emotional investment because the audience begins supplying part of the experience," Probst says. Binge-watching builds momentum, but appointment viewing makes fans sit with the emotion.

Physical water coolers may be no more, but modern appointment viewing shows are fighting the impatience of binge watchers, and they're winning.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Was a ‘Proud’ Producer Behind “Buffy the Vampire Slayer”: ‘That Little Show Did Great’
articles.summary: “I was very excited about the show. That little show did great,” the country music legend said of the beloved series, on which she was an executive producer
articles.body:
Dolly Parton died at age 80 on Tuesday, Aug. 25

One of the many projects the singer was involved in during her career was the hit series Buffy the Vampire Slayer, on which she is credited as an executive producer

"That little show did great," Parton once said

Dolly Parton played a role in one of the biggest TV hits of the late '90s.

The country music legend, who died at age 80 on Aug. 25 , was at one point "very involved" behind the scenes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer , the Sarah Michelle Gellar –led series that ran for seven seasons from 1997 to 2003.

"A lot of my work was done just conversing back and forth with the business people there. And I'd go out for meetings now and then," Parton told Business Insider in 2024. She is listed as an executive producer on the series but told the outlet, "I have to give more people credit on Buffy the Vampire Slayer than me. A lot of people did so much work on that."

"I was very excited about the show. That little show did great," Parton said.

She added that "didn't get to meet all of" the cast, "but I wanted them to know that I was there for them, I was proud of them, and they were doing a great job."

Gellar, 49, previously spoke about Parton's involvement in the series, calling it a "little-known fact" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in 2023.

"The legend Dolly Parton was a producer," Gellar said. "We never saw her [but] we'd get Christmas gifts in the beginning that would have our name, and I would think, 'She doesn't even know who I am.' And then one day, someone asked her about it, and she complimented the show and my performance. I was like, 'Oh, I can die now. Dolly Parton knows who I am and thinks I'm good.'"

After news of Parton's death, Gellar wrote on Instagram, "Just being a small part of the great history of @dollyparton is everything to me," and shared a clip of the singer talking about Buffy on Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen in 2021.

In that clip, Parton explained that her production company with former manager Sandy Gallin, Sandollar Productions, helped with Buffy . "We were a small part of that. I was very, very proud to be part of that," she told host Cohen at the time.

The news of Parton's death was announced in a video by her nephew Bryan Seaver. "I'm representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next. This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now. It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness."

"My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly, but so have you. She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family whether you liked it or not. Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever. Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, she farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest," her nephew continued.

"Rest in peace, Aunt Dolly — Aunt, Granny, Gigi. May God bless Dolly Parton, and may God bless you all. She will always love you."

The legendary singer's death came four days after she told PEOPLE she was "dealing with some health issues that I just didn't pay attention to when I was watching over Carl ," referring to her late husband, Carl Dean , who died in 2025.

"Even though I'm still healin', I'm still workin'! You know me — as I've often said — I've dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I'm gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life," she said.

articles.title: Why the Projection for the Houston Rockets to Earn the 3rd Seed in the West is Realistic
articles.summary: The projection of Houston finishing with a 51-31 record is achievable for a few reasons.
articles.body:
On August 24, 2026, ESPN revealed its projected standings for the upcoming 2026-27. ESPN projected the Houston Rockets to finish as the third seed, tied with the Denver Nuggets . Both teams would finish with a 51-31 record.

Considering that the Rockets finished the last two seasons with a 52-30 record, these projections are reasonable. Along with Houston's recent roster additions, the development of the young core, and the return of injured players, the third seed seems achievable if not likely.

Houston signed Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanović from free agency this summer, adding much-needed roster depth and veteran leadership. Smart's strong and motivating locker-room presence, ball-handling and playmaking skills, and elite perimeter defense will improve the second unit. Bogdanović's signing adds a three-point threat to the team, which the Rockets lacked last season.Houston has a very strong young core.

Amen Thompson has developed into one of the best young two-way players in the NBA. Thompson's length and speed make him one of the most versatile perimeter defenders. He also has a strong interior presence. Out of his average of 18.3 points per game, 12.1 of those points came directly in the paint. His athleticism and creativity make him an elite finisher in the paint, which is proven by his 70.5% field goal percentage in the restricted area.

Amen Thompson's weakness is his three-point and mid-range shooting, in which he averaged an abysmal 21.6% and 27.8%, respectively. However, Houston hired Chip Engelland to improve the team's shooting. Engelland's track record shows that he can work his magic and make Thompson a respectable shooter.

Engelland will also focus on improving the 24-year-old Alperen Şengün. Şengün shot a poor 30.5% from deep and 35.5% from mid-range. On top of this, he also averages 69.1% from the free-throw line.

If Engelland can improve their shooting, it will force the opposing teams to spread out to the perimeter, thereby creating space in the paint and widening the cutting lanes.

Houston's roster will also be bolstered by the addition of both Steven Adams and Fred VanVleet . VanVleet missed the entire 2025-26 season due to an ACL tear, but is now healthy and increasingly motivated for the upcoming season. Adams suffered a severe ankle sprain in January, missing the rest of the season.

These improvements to the Rockets' roster should be enough to land them in the top five of the Western Conference. Pinnacle has the over/under for Houston's total season wins at 47.5, meaning that the team will have to perform only slightly above the sharp predictions to earn the third seed and win 51 games.

The indication is that although the prediction is not probable, it is certainly realistic. Will the improvements in the roster and management be enough?

articles.title: ‘AGT’ Recap: Who Got Mel B.’s Live Golden Buzzer?
articles.summary: Night two of the Live Shows featured 11 more acts hitting the stage for a shot at the Semifinals.
articles.body:
The Quarterfinals continued on the August 25 episode of America's Got Talent . Eleven more acts took the stage in hopes of moving on in the competition.

Like last week, there was one Live Golden Buzzer in play. After Howie Mandel gave his to Hundred Fingers on August 18, sending them straight to the Finals, the power was in Mel B. 's hands this time around. America will vote for their favorites of the rest of the contestants, and three of those acts will move onto the Semifinals during tomorrow night's results show.

Because Simon Cowell is away from the show for a few weeks due to a "routine" procedure relating to his back injury , his seat was left empty, leaving Mandel, Mel, and Sofia Vergara to offer commentary from the judges' table.

Scroll down for a recap of the night's performances and to find out who got the Golden Buzzer.

Kicking off the night was LaRussell with a rap performance, accompanied by his friends from the Bay Area.

"First of all, I love what you guys stand for. I can feel the energy literally bouncing off the stage," Mel B. said. "I did find it a little bit chaotic. There was a lot going on. But like I said, your energy was right up there. It was. And that's the part that I enjoyed. I almost wish you had a few more days to rehearse it. I felt like you were a little bit out of breath, but I could feel the excitement."

The audience boo-ed Mel's response, but Vergara jumped in to say, "I do think this was a step up from the audition. I love it. I think it's amazing what they do." Finally, Mandel added, "I think it was good, I think it was entertaining. I don't know if it's at the level Season 21 is looking for. It felt like a musical recital from a high school to me."

The second performance was from aerialist Veronika Goroshkova, who was one of Vergara's Golden Buzzers during the Auditions. She did another wild routine, this time set to Taylor Swift 's "The Fate of Ophelia."

"Now you know why I gave her the Golden Buzzer. There is no one like her," Vergara raved. "The fascinating thing about me for you is you make it seem so easy, so effortless."

Mandel called Veronika "amazing" and said no other aerialist on the show has been as "graceful" as her. Mel B. added, "What else can I say? Everybody's said everything. You were that powerful, the sponge of my microphone popped off. Graceful. Just brilliant."

Just days after celebrating her 18th birthday, Bety hit the stage for a performance of TK TK. Bety was one of Mel B.'s callback acts who made the Quarterfinals after her second chance performance, and now her fate is in America's hands.

Bety sang Sam Smith's "Fire on Fire" for the Live Show. "You know I'm a massive fan of yours. Your voice is like velvet," Mel said. "I do think you played it a little bit too safe tonight. I know your vocal range is so wide, but it was beautiful."

Vergara told Bety she already looks like a "big star" on stage. "You wanted to do this your whole life and it shows in your performance. I love it," she gushed. Meanwhile, Mandel said Bety is "one of the best singers" on the season, but admitted, "That song doesn't have a ton of range. You have a ton of range. I love your audition so much more than this."

Come Here, a dance group, took the stage next. Heading into the big night, the group dealt with some setbacks as their choreographer had a prior commitment and couldn't make it to L.A. until just 12 hours before showtime.

The routine got a standing ovation from all three judges. "What a unique blend of contemporary and ballet, very original choreography," Mandel said. "You're amazing, you deserve to be here."

Vergara added, "Breathtaking. It was amazing. It was perfection. No tricks, no flips, it's just a unit." Mel B. said she thought the routine was "absolutely incredible," and it even seemed like she was going to press the Golden Buzzer for a second after a brief side conversation with Mandel. However, she held off for a future performance.

Music duo Nyjah Music and Zyah Rhythm were one of Cowell's callback acts. They came to the Live Shows hoping to show a new level of confidence with a performance of "I Swear."

The judges cringed through the performance, and Mel B. even hit her red buzzer to signify that she was not impressed. "You guys can sing, you can harmonize," Mandel began. "I think Simon said it in the package and I think he's right … it takes experience and time. I think you're going to be great. I think you're going to do well. But I feel it's just about experience. The nerves are kind of showing."

Mel B. said, "I actually felt I did you a favor. I think you need a lot more time, a lot more experience, and at this point in the competition, this should be your best. I should be able to feel the hunger, the passion. It was just like you were taking a walk on Malibu beach without a care in the world. I didn't see it." She urged the guys to practice and come back with "more determination."

Vergara had to agree with Mel and Mandel that Nyjah and Zyah played it too safe and needed more experience. "I think you need to keep working and follow your dream because you guys are good," she concluded.

Magician Geno Ploeger was up next. After previously working with AGT winner Mat Franco, Geno is now ready to make a name for himself. Mandel warned him during his audition that he needed to do something more original, and he came ready to show that off.

"I don't even have words," Mel B. said afterwards. Vergara raved, "This was original. I'm so glad you paid attention to what Howie told you. This feels like you. It suits you. This is how you have to keep doing it."

Finally, Mandel gushed, "I said if you come back, you do you, something I have never seen. You. Did. You."

Cowell called Patrox "one of the most original acts we've ever seen" when he auditioned, and he showed off his unique backwards dance skills once again.

"I think it's so clever what you do. I don't really fully understand what the hell is happening, but it's fun," Vergara said. "To make something like that work on a stage like this is not easy."

Mel B. admitted she liked that Patrox is "so excited," but again, she said she didn't understand the concept of his dancing and backwards replay. Mandel jumped in to say, "I think what you do is incredibly unique. It's a trick. It's an amazing trick. I applaud you."

Teenage rocker Nene Royal took the stage next. After getting through to the Quarterfinals as one of Mandel's callback acts, she was ready to prove she belonged, especially since her audition went so viral.

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq — AGT Time Podcast (@agttimepod) August 26, 2026

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq

After Nene's performance of "Black Hole Sun" by Soundgarden, Mandel addressed NBC directly, saying, "Give her the $1 million. Right now!" Vergara said, "I think you can really win this competition. You can sing and play that guitar. No wonder everybody on the street asks me about you!"

Mel could barely get a word in edgewise over the loud screams of the audience. "You are just the most humblest, sweet, young lady, and then you come out on this stage and it's a different vibe," she applauded.

Vergara urged her to push the Golden Buzzer, and Mel B. said, "I love really good vocals. I'm a 90s girl. I'm into pop music. That kind of music is not my vibe. But your vocals are on point, your guitar is on point, your look, your energy, your vibe … how could I not do this?!" And with that, Nene is in the Finals!

Mackenzie Sol , one of Mel B.'s audition Golden Buzzers, returned to the stage next. He wanted to do something different for the Live Shows, so he sang Tate McRae's "You Broke Me First," and got emotional at the end of the performance.

"That was so good," Mel B. promised. "That was everything. The feelings, the trills, the vocals, the voice, the everything. That was just … yeah." Vergara told Mackenzie, "I think the girls are going to go crazy with you. So handsome, such a beautiful energy, such a beautiful voice. I loved your audition and I love you tonight."

Mandel said she hopes people vote for Mackenzie, and Mel jumped in to add, "I really, really, really hope people vote for you!" Mandel also made sure Mackenzie knew he "rose to the occasion" of having to perform after Nene.

Extreme danger act (and married couple) Brad and Tracy came with another death-defying routine next. Mel was so grossed out by Brad's sword-swallowing trick that she pushed her red buzzer and turned away.

The act did not quite resonate and fell very flat, although Mandel did give a standing ovation. "The energy and the showmanship … you cant even put into words what we just saw," he said. "It is so bad, it is amazing."

Vergara added, "I could not stop thinking about what your neighbors think about you two. You guys are scary. Tracy, you should be in a scary movie. You're perfect, your acting, your delivery. It's amazing. I don't know if this is good, if it's bad. We can't stop looking at you guys, so I guess it's a good thing."

Mel admitted that "this is a genre where people do things to themselves like that," but said, "I find it more comedic. I do like the vibe. But just … why?"

The final performance of the night was from singing duo Butter and Grit.

"Your vocals have got exponentially more than amazing. That song, and it's an original … I love your friendship, I love your vibe, America needs to vote for you," Mel B. gushed.

What Is 'AGT' Finalist Preacher Lawson Doing Now?

Vergara said she loved Butter and Grit's original songs. "They feel like they're already hits, that they've been hits. I really love your friendship and relationship," she added. Mandel concluded, "There's nothing more America than that type of music and the way you sing it."

America's Got Talent , Season 21, Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 8/7c, NBC
